hints: Think about what information is preserved in a stem-and-leaf diagram versus what is lost in a box-and-whisker plot.
A box-and-whisker plot only displays a 5-number summary (minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum).
A stem-and-leaf diagram preserves the individual original raw data values, allowing calculation of other statistics such as the mean, mode, or standard deviation.
walkthrough: State the main advantage: A stem-and-leaf diagram retains all the original raw data values, whereas a box-and-whisker plot only displays summary statistics (the 5-number summary).
Alternatively: It allows other statistical measures, such as the mean, mode, or standard deviation, to be calculated directly from the diagram.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Compare the nature of the two diagrams.
- A box-and-whisker plot is a summary representation that displays only five key statistics: minimum value, lower quartile ($Q_1$), median ($Q_2$), upper quartile ($Q_3$), and maximum value. Individual data points cannot be recovered from it.
- A stem-and-leaf diagram displays every single individual observation in the dataset while still giving an overview of the shape of the distribution.

Step 2: Formulate the advantage clearly.
State that a stem-and-leaf diagram retains all original (raw) data values, or that it allows further statistical calculations that cannot be performed using a box-and-whisker plot (such as finding the mean, mode, frequency, or standard deviation).

ai_rubric.Comparing Statistical Representations: States that a stem-and-leaf diagram retains all raw data or allows calculating mean, mode, frequency, or standard deviation.

hints: Set up a central vertical stem with values covering all heights from 170s to 210s: stems are 17, 18, 19, 20, 21.
Place Amazons on the left-hand side and Giants on the right-hand side.
Remember that leaves on the left-hand side (Amazons) must be ordered from right to left (increasing away from the stem).
Include a clear key that identifies both teams and includes the unit 'cm': for example, $1 \mid 18 \mid 2$ means 181 cm for Amazons and 182 cm for Giants.
walkthrough: Determine the central stems covering the range 175 cm to 215 cm: stems are 17, 18, 19, 20, 21.

Order the leaves for Amazons on the left (ordered right-to-left away from the stem):
- Stem 17: 8 (178)
- Stem 18: 4 2 1 (181, 182, 184)
- Stem 19: 8 6 0 (190, 196, 198)
- Stem 20: 5 2 1 (201, 202, 205)

Order the leaves for Giants on the right (ordered left-to-right away from the stem):
- Stem 17: 5 (175)
- Stem 18: 2 4 7 9 (182, 184, 187, 189)
- Stem 19: 2 3 5 5 5 (192, 193, 195, 195, 195)
- Stem 20: 4 (204)
- Stem 21: (no leaves)

Construct the back-to-back diagram with a key:
$$\begin{array}{rcccl}
\textbf{Amazons} & & \textbf{Stem} & & \textbf{Giants} \\
\hline
8 & | & 17 & | & 5 \\
4 \quad 2 \quad 1 & | & 18 & | & 2 \quad 4 \quad 7 \quad 9 \\

$$\text{Key: } 1 \mid 18 \mid 2 \text{ means } 181\text{ cm for Amazons and } 182\text{ cm for Giants}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Choose the stem and leaves.
The heights range from 175 cm to 215 cm. The first two digits form the stem ($17, 18, 19, 20, 21$) and the last digit forms the leaf (units digit in cm).

Step 2: Sort the data for both teams.
- Amazons heights (11 players):
  178, 181, 182, 184, 190, 196, 198, 201, 202, 205, 215
- Giants heights (11 players):
  175, 182, 184, 187, 189, 192, 193, 195, 195, 195, 204

Step 3: Arrange the leaves on the back-to-back diagram.
- For Amazons on the left: Place leaves increasing from right to left, moving away from the stem line.
  * Stem 17: 8
  * Stem 18: 4, 2, 1 (written as 4 2 1 so 1 is nearest the stem)
  * Stem 19: 8, 6, 0 (written as 8 6 0 so 0 is nearest the stem)
  * Stem 20: 5, 2, 1 (written as 5 2 1 so 1 is nearest the stem)
  * Stem 21: 5
- For Giants on the right: Place leaves increasing from left to right, moving away from the stem line.
  * Stem 17: 5
  * Stem 18: 2 4 7 9
  * Stem 19: 2 3 5 5 5
  * Stem 20: 4
  * Stem 21: empty

Step 4: Provide a complete key.
The key must explain leaves on both sides and include units:
$$\text{Key: } 1 \mid 18 \mid 2 \text{ means } 181\text{ cm for Amazons and } 182\text{ cm for Giants}$$

ai_rubric.Constructing Stem-and-Leaf Diagrams: Draws correct back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram with stem 17-21, correctly ordered leaves on both sides, and a complete key with units.

hints: List the 11 heights for the Amazons in ascending order: 178, 181, 182, 184, 190, 196, 198, 201, 202, 205, 215.
Find the lower quartile $Q_1$, which is the 3rd value in the ordered list: $Q_1 = 182$ cm.
Find the upper quartile $Q_3$, which is the 9th value in the ordered list: $Q_3 = 202$ cm.
Calculate the interquartile range: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 202 - 182$.
walkthrough:
List the ordered heights of the 11 Amazons players in ascending order:
$$178, \quad 181, \quad 182, \quad 184, \quad 190, \quad 196, \quad 198, \quad 201, \quad 202, \quad 205, \quad 215$$

Identify the positions of the quartiles for $n = 11$:
- The median is the 6th value: $196$ cm.
- The lower quartile $Q_1$ is the 3rd value: $Q_1 = 182$ cm.
- The upper quartile $Q_3$ is the 9th value: $Q_3 = 202$ cm.

Compute the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 202 - 182 = 20\text{ cm}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Write down the ordered dataset for Amazons.
From the stem-and-leaf diagram, list all 11 player heights in order:
$$178, 181, 182, 184, 190, 196, 198, 201, 202, 205, 215$$

Step 2: Determine the positions of the quartiles.
For a dataset of size $n = 11$:
- The median ($Q_2$) is the $\frac{11 + 1}{2} = 6$th value: $196$ cm.
- The lower half of the data consists of the 5 values below the median: $178, 181, 182, 184, 190$.
  The lower quartile $Q_1$ is the middle value of this lower half (the 3rd overall value):
  $$Q_1 = 182\text{ cm}$$
- The upper half of the data consists of the 5 values above the median: $198, 201, 202, 205, 215$.
  The upper quartile $Q_3$ is the middle value of this upper half (the 9th overall value):
  $$Q_3 = 202\text{ cm}$$

Step 3: Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 202 - 182 = 20\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Calculating the Interquartile Range: Identifies Q1 = 182 and Q3 = 202 and subtracts to find IQR = 20 cm.

hints: Find the sum of the heights of the original 11 Amazons players by adding all 11 values from the stem-and-leaf diagram: $\Sigma_{11} = 2132$ cm.
Four new players join, so the team now has $11 + 4 = 15$ players, with a new mean height of $191.2$ cm.
Calculate the new total sum of heights for all 15 players: $\Sigma_{15} = 15 \times 191.2 = 2868$ cm.
Set up an equation equating the new sum to the original sum plus the heights of the four new players ($180 + 185 + 190 + h$), and solve for $h$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the sum of the heights of the original 11 Amazons players:
$$\Sigma_{11} = 178 + 181 + 182 + 184 + 190 + 196 + 198 + 201 + 202 + 205 + 215 = 2132\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the total height of all 15 players using the new mean:
$$\Sigma_{15} = 15 \times 191.2 = 2868\text{ cm}$$

Let $h$ be the height of the fourth new player. Form an equation using the known heights of the other three new players ($180, 185, 190$ cm):
$$\Sigma_{11} + 180 + 185 + 190 + h = 2868$$
$$2132 + 555 + h = 2868$$
$$2687 + h = 2868$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Calculate the sum of heights of the original 11 Amazons players.
Using the heights from the stem-and-leaf diagram:
$$\Sigma_{11} = 178 + 181 + 182 + 184 + 190 + 196 + 198 + 201 + 202 + 205 + 215 = 2132\text{ cm}$$

Step 2: Calculate the required total sum of all 15 players.
When 4 new players join, the total number of players becomes $11 + 4 = 15$.
The new mean height is given as $191.2$ cm.
Using the formula $\text{Total} = n \times \bar{x}$:
$$\Sigma_{15} = 15 \times 191.2 = 2868\text{ cm}$$

Step 3: Set up an equation with the fourth player's height $h$.
The heights of three of the new players are $180$ cm, $185$ cm, and $190$ cm. The sum of these three heights is:
$$180 + 185 + 190 = 555\text{ cm}$$
Now add the original 11 players and the 4 new players:
$$\Sigma_{15} = \Sigma_{11} + 555 + h$$
$$2868 = 2132 + 555 + h$$
$$2868 = 2687 + h$$

Step 4: Solve for $h$:
$$h = 2868 - 2687 = 181\text{ cm}$$
The height of the fourth new player is $181$ cm.

ai_rubric.Calculating a Mean from Raw Data: Finds sum(11) = 2132, sum(15) = 2868, and solves 2132 + 180 + 185 + 190 + h = 2868 to obtain h = 181 cm.
